edge.dataCrossing: fingerprints: sha256(version, rule, repo, scope, subject, codeText(line))
edge.contract: a line edit changes the fingerprint; code moving above it does not
edge.failureModes: measured: rewording the sink (CALL "SYSTEM" for CALL 'SYSTEM') changes f325f4f3 to aefb6038 with the route intact; moving the sink into a PERFORMed paragraph changes it to d6cfbacb, because the scope changes. Level 2 pairing (text removed) catches the first and not the second; level 3 (rule, program, source statement) catches both
edge.attackSurface: a patch that makes the target look resolved by editing its line

fractal.siblingConsistency: HOLDS - baseline matching keys on fingerprint and rule (diff.mjs baselineChange), the same identity
fractal.scaleUp: BREAKS - two findings of one rule in one paragraph with one subject share a level 2 key; pairing them against a single remaining head finding reads a fixed target as still reported
fractal.scaleDown: HOLDS - checked routes are stamped by the same function (scan.mjs:152); an allow-list the patch adds leaves the route in checked under the base fingerprint f325f4f3, so cleared-by-check is an exact match
fractal.mirrorTest: HOLDS - both trees are stamped by one implementation

edge.dataCrossing: the base finding, the head's findings and checked list, the changed lines
edge.contract: pass only on a disappearance the gate can explain
edge.failureModes: statement-removed as drafted accepts a line 'reworded and no longer flagged'. A reword the engine stops recognising as a sink reads as a fix. Measured: OS_COMMAND_ROUTINE is case-insensitive (dataflow.mjs:17) and double quotes stay flagged, so the obvious rewords of CALL 'SYSTEM' do not escape - but the outcome rests on every sink recogniser having no such gap, which nothing checks. The flow engine can list every sink it knows, reached or not (dataflow.mjs:1353, opts.listSinks), which turns the outcome into a count: the sinks of the target's kind in its program went down
edge.attackSurface: a drafter, or a hostile patch, that rewrites the sink statement into a form no recogniser holds

fractal.siblingConsistency: BREAKS - cleared-by-check rests on an engine fact (checked); statement-removed as drafted rests on a text fact (a changed line). The two should rest on the same kind of evidence
fractal.scaleDown: BREAKS - trace hops carry program, item, file and via, but no line (flow.mjs trace construction); a route cut in the middle - the MOVE between source and sink deleted - cannot be attributed to a changed line, and lands in gone-unexplained. The spec does not say so
fractal.mirrorTest: HOLDS - source-removed is the mirror of statement-removed, and needs the same count (no source listing exists yet; listSinks has no sources twin)

edge.dataCrossing: sentences built from rule ids, rule text, paths, lines, severities, counts
edge.contract: no finding detail, no source text
edge.failureModes: a path is text the repository chose: a file named for an instruction reaches the model through the reasons. printable() removes control and bidirectional characters, not words
edge.attackSurface: prompt injection into the drafter through file names

fractal.siblingConsistency: HOLDS - explain's packet already goes through commitwork's untrusted-text envelope; the reasons must be named as the same kind of text

edge.dataCrossing: program files the patch changed, copybook directories
edge.contract: compiler from outside the tree; working directory outside the repository; regression only
edge.failureModes: a copybook edit changes no program file, so 'each program file the patch changed' compiles nothing for the change most likely to break a compile. Measured elsewhere: diff exists because a one-line copybook edit rewrites every program that COPYs it (diff.mjs:18-22)
edge.attackSurface: cwd-first executable search on Windows for a bare name; the spec resolves to an absolute path, which closes it

fractal.scaleUp: BREAKS - see failureModes: copybook-driven programs are not in the compile set
fractal.mirrorTest: HOLDS - base and head compiled alike

boundaries.name: scans under the memory guard -> verdict (spec S4 coverage, G-I6)

edge.failureModes: the guard reads whole-machine free memory, so the same inputs can give undecided on one run and pass on the next; G-I6 as written claims identical documents unconditionally. Measured: removing a copybook the program copies sets coverageIncomplete and a compile-set coverage entry, which is a buildable witness for G2.6; the memory reserve is not, since the reader is process-global (lib/kernel/memory.mjs setMemoryReaders)

fractal.siblingConsistency: HOLDS - diff ORs both sides' coverage (diff.mjs summary)

edge.dataCrossing: file text of base and head
edge.contract: in process; lines compared as the fingerprint compares them
edge.failureModes: an edit-distance cap is stated (5,000) without the memory it implies; Myers' trace is quadratic in D. A renumbered sequence area would mark every line changed if lines were compared raw, which is why the codeText comparison matters
edge.attackSurface: a patch built to exhaust memory in the diff

phase2_fractalAtam.corePattern: the model proposes and a deterministic gate disposes; what the tool cannot establish is reported as undecided, never as clean
phase2_fractalAtam.macro: CONSISTENT - the gate is diff plus a verdict, as explain is a report plus source; one more command over the same two-tree machinery
phase2_fractalAtam.meso: BROKEN at S5 - outcomes rest on two kinds of evidence (engine facts for cleared-by-check, text facts for statement-removed and source-removed). Making all three rest on the engine is the fix and costs one symmetric sources listing
phase2_fractalAtam.micro: CONSISTENT - reasons, exit codes and the untrusted envelope follow explain and diff

tradeoffs.gain: a crash is never read as a fail, and the CLI keeps one exit-code rule
tradeoffs.cost: a caller reading exit codes alone passes everything (F5)
tradeoffs.resolution: keep, and add --exit-code, which exits 1 on fail and 3 on undecided

tradeoffs.gain: no laundering through an unattributable change
tradeoffs.cost: a real fix (the MOVE removed) goes to a person
tradeoffs.resolution: keep; say why in the reason, and prefer checks in fix recipes

tradeoffs.gain: a missing copy library cannot fail a good patch
tradeoffs.cost: a program that never compiled is never checked
